title: GPU thermal-triggered slowdown investigation notes
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the on-call investigation notes from the 2026-02-09 midday degradation affecting a subset of Dedicated GPU pools (west-1a). Symptoms were a sudden increase in p95/p99 token latency and sustained throughput drop for ~45–90 minutes, correlated with GPU thermal excursions and downstream throttling. Unlike typical noisy-tenant CPU spikes, the signal here was thermal-induced clock throttling that propagated to tenant-level latency — we walked through triage, tentative hypotheses, short-term mitigations, and proposed runbook deltas.

Why this is different: thermal-triggered slowdowns previously were thought to be rare because datacenter cooling metrics looked normal. This incident shows that aggregated pod placement + localized rack cooling imbalance + device firmware behavior can produce a latent condition that triggers widespread small-slowdowns without obvious host-level eviction.

High-level timeline (timestamps UTC):
- 12:04 — First alert: Dedicated pool west-1a p95 token latency > 1200ms, throughput -18% (alert SLO-DED-POOL-THROUGHPUT).
- 12:06 — Pager duty to SRE on-call (Samir). Quick check: autoscaler stable, pod counts unchanged.
- 12:08 — NVML thermal events stream shows rising GPU temperature on 4 nodes (gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-11,gpu-14) crossing 84C.
- 12:11 — p99 spikes correlated to requests routed to those specific nodes (trace IDs), KV cache hit-rate unchanged (so not cache thrash).
- 12:15 — ssh into gpu-07: nvidia-smi shows clocks dropping from 1740MHz -> 1370MHz under sustained load; dmesg shows repeated firmware thermal warnings.
- 12:20 — Decision: enable short-term routing exclusion for nodes reporting thermal throttling (automated node cordon + route-away policy applied).
- 12:24 — Immediate p95 improved to 700–800ms, throughput partially restored to -8% baseline.
- 12:40 — Rack-level AHU telemetry shows a drop in chilled-water flow to rack-4 for 20 minutes starting 11:58 — suggests cooling transient.
- 13:10 — Nodes begin to cool, clocks return to expected ranges; routing exclusion lifted at 13:14 after 3 consecutive health checks OK.
- 13:30 — Post-incident: overall metrics returned to baseline, but we observed intermittent small increases in tail latencies for ~2 hours.

Primary signals checked:
- NVML thermal events (nvidia-smi dmon / nvml API)
- GPU clock frequencies and utilization
- dmesg/kernel logs for GPU firmware warnings
- Rack PDUs and chiller telemetry (via onprem infra API)
- Autoscaler decisions (no scale events)
- Per-request routing traces to attribute latency to nodes

Immediate hypothesis space (ranked):
1) Localized cooling transient caused GPUs to hit thermal throttle point -> device-level clocks reduced -> per-token inference slower and batching effectiveness changed. (Most likely)
2) A firmware update pushed to a subset of nodes altered thermal guard curves, making them throttle earlier. (Possible — check fleet rollout logs.)
3) Noisy neighbor with pathological kernel causing hotter sustained power draw on specific GPUs — but utilization profiles do not match this (utilization steady). (Less likely)
4) NVLink or PCIe errors causing occasional stall and higher instruction latency; logs did not show ECC errors. (Low likelihood for this event)

Reproduction attempts and lab notes:
- Replayed a representative benchmark (batched transformer inference at the same QPS) on an isolated test node while throttling the local simulated ambient (heat gun not used — but fan curves modified via ipmi) and observed clock stepping behavior and ~20–35% per-token latency increase when clocks drop ~20%.
- Reproduced same effect in our rack-level testbed by restricting fan speed and inflating inlet temperature by 6–8C; GPUs on the testbench showed NVML thermal warnings and reduced clocks to levels consistent with production nodes.
- No firmware-level log differences observed between affected and unaffected nodes in the short-term triage; scheduled a deeper fleet comparison (see action items).

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Automated routing exclusions (routing policy flagged nodes with NVML temp > 82C and persistent clock drops > 200MHz for 30s).
- No immediate cluster-wide scale-up — decided not to trigger scale because thermal condition could make new nodes also vulnerable if rack cooling is transient.
- Ops notified infra-runner team to check rack chiller and PDU feed for anomalies; on-call infra acknowledged a transient chiller imbalance and manually adjusted flow to rack-4.

Runbook déltas proposed (draft):
- Add a thermal-specific triage checklist to SRE oncall runbook: quick nvidia-smi checks, NVML event stream query, rack-chiller correlator query, immediate routing exclusion threshold values.
- New gating rule for routing exclusion: NVML temperature >= 82C AND sustained clock drop >= 150MHz for 45s -> auto-cordon + route-away.
- Add a green/amber/red thermostat for racks in the console UI (amber if any node in rack crosses 78C).
- Avoid automatic autoscaler triggers for Dedicated pools when >3 nodes in a rack report thermal amber within 10 minutes — otherwise scale can mask root cause without resolving cooling.
- Documented manual override steps for infra to temporarily increase chilled-water flow and a checklist for verifying chiller valves.

Observability enhancements (short list):
- Add GPU clock frequency timeseries per node to the Dedicated pool dashboards with 1s granularity for 30m windows around alerts.
- Surface NVML thermal event counts as a first-class signal in alerting rules (not just GPU_utilization).
- Correlate route table and request traces with node thermal labels so latency SLO alerts show candidate thermal culprits.

Longer-term remediation ideas (backlog):
- Fleet firmware audit: compare thermals and guard-curve config across images and recent firmware pushes (owner: firmware-eng, ticket DED-2093).
- Placement logic: avoid concentrating hot-running tenants in same rack when inlet temp trending high; use anti-affinity heuristics sensitive to rack thermal history (owner: serving-runtime placement team).
- Pre-warm policy: add a conservative clock/thermal warm-up handshake for bursty workloads to avoid immediate hitting of thermal throttle under burst.
- Infrastructure: collaborate with data center ops to tune rack cooling and add more granular flow telemetry hooking into our console.

Action items (owners + tentative dates):
- SRE: formalize runbook thermal section + test emergency cordon logic in staging (owner Samir, due 2026-03-01).
- Infra: inspect rack-4 chiller logs for 2026-02-09 11:45–12:30 and confirm valve state (owner Ava Chen, due 2026-02-16, ticket JIRA:SRE-4127).
- Fleet: produce firmware delta report comparing images for affected nodes (owner Diego Martinez, due 2026-03-05, ticket JIRA:DED-2093).
- Observability: add GPU clock timeseries widget and NVML event metric (owner Rhea Kapoor, due 2026-03-12).

Notes for on-call playbook update (practical commands and quick checks):
- Check top-level alert with timeframe, e.g., query: metrics:dedicated_pool_latency{pool=\"west-1a\",quantile=\"p95\"} offset 15m
- Quick node-level thermal check: ssh node && sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.sm --format=csv -l 2
- NVML event tail: curl -s \"http://fleet-metrics/api/nvml/events?node=gpu-07&since=15m\"
- Rack cooling: infra-api get rack-telemetry rack-4 --window 30m
- Temporary mitigation: route-control cordon-node gpu-07 --reason thermal-throttle && route-control drain-requests --node gpu-07 --grace 10s

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What changed between nodes that made only 4/20 nodes hit the throttle point? (fleet configs, subtle manufacturing variance, or placement?)
- Should autoscaler be blocked by a thermal safety policy automatically? We currently rely on human-in-loop for infra actions — need policy decision on automation vs risk.
- Do we need dedicated thermal simulation tests in CI for every firmware/driver update?

Appendix: Raw snippets pulled during triage (redacted):
- nvidia-smi snippet: \"GPU 0 Temp: 86C Pwr: 320W Clocks SM: 1370 MHz\"
- dmesg: \"[gpu-fw] thermal_protect: entering reduction_mode, target_clock 1370MHz\"
- Slack callout: <@Ava> saw chiller valve oscillation on rack-4 around 11:58; manual bump at 12:22 restored flow.

If you touched this doc: add any additional logs, timelines, or failed reproduction experiments below. We should convert to a canonical postmortem if we confirm firmware or placement as root cause.

-- Samir
